newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds post decline after low April CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds post decline after low April CPI.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed lower on Sunday as CPI-linked bonds were pulled down by April's lower-than-expected consumer price index, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: -0.21 pct to 106.44
* CPI-linked government bonds: -0.35 pct to 106.53
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.35 pct to 106.74
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.28 pct to 105.01
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.16 to 105.37
Volume including Makams was 130 million shekels.
"There was an excess supply of CPI-linked bonds because of the low consumer price index and expectations that future CPIs will be low as well," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.

The April CPI of 0.7 percent, which was published on Thursday after the close of the trading day, was well below analysts' forecasts of about 1.1 percent and marked a comparative slowing of inflation from February and March.
"Prices of CPI-linked bonds fell fairly sharply, especially short- and medium-term bonds, while yields were up," he said.
"There was good demand for unlinked bonds with surplus demand...spread evenly among Makams and the other unlinked bonds," Halpern said.
"In coming days, prices of CPI-linked bonds will continue to fall while demand will be up for unlinked bonds," said an investment manager at Jerusalem Capital Markets.
"In the long run we expect inflation to come down as a result of the slowdown in the economy and thus demand for unlinked bonds will continue," he said.

"Demand for unlinked bonds will continue in the coming days until the market reaches a new balance, depending on inflation expectations and on the interest rate. The market expects a small cut of 0.3 percentage point at the end of May," said Halpern.
The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut its interest rate to 13.9 percent at the end of February.
Trading in dollar-linked bonds was mixed, traders said with prices falling slightly.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.39 shekels)
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
